query: What best-practice consent language, de-identification steps, and tiered data-access governance models are recommended for ethically sharing EEG plus continuous emotion datasets?

response.query: What best-practice consent language, de-identification steps, and tiered data-access governance models are recommended for ethically sharing EEG plus continuous emotion datasets?
response.answer: Best-practice consent language should clearly explain EEG and emotion data use. De-identification should remove all personal identifiers. Tiered data-access governance models should enforce strict access controls based on user roles.

results.title: Nested Learning in Higher Education: Integrating ...
results.content: Nested Learning is thus not a generic label for any AI-enhanced course, but a specific configuration that: (i) integrates generative AI agents, neuroeducational protocols and smart-campus data in a unified orchestration layer; (ii) foregrounds cognitive safety, self-regulated learning and a Pedagogy of Hope as explicit sustainability goals; and (iii) treats learner trajectories as dynamical processes to be guided, rather than as static outcomes to be measured. **Core contribution.** This paper proposes Nested Learning as a policy-aware orchestration framework for AI-rich higher education: rather than treating generative AI as a stand-alone tool, Nested Learning coordinates layered supports (teacher–agents–peers–context) under explicit governance constraints to sustain engagement, self-regulation, and cognitive safety over time [45,46]. Phase 1 suggests that Nested Learning micro-events can be tracked through robust P300 markers using affordable EEG; Phase 2 shows that Nested Learning and neuroadaptive adjustments are strongly associated with engagement and self-regulation, both quantitatively and qualitatively; and the technical–ethical analysis underscores that sustaining such an ecosystem in higher education requires careful balancing of technical performance and protection of learners’ rights.
